title: September 2026 arXiv physics: precision signals and testable proposals

sections.title: MAGGIE: A Magnetic Gravitational Wave Induction Experiment
sections.abstract: The authors propose a high-frequency gravitational-wave detector using a 14 T solenoid, a symmetry-matched pickup loop and noise-rejection readout, with projected sensitivity into the kHz–MHz regime.
sections.claimed_result: The design study projects strain spectral noise density of about 4 × 10⁻¹⁶/√Hz at 40 MHz for transient searches and strain near 10⁻¹⁹ for a year-long continuous search; these are projections, not detections.
sections.evidence_type: forecast/proposal; detector design and sensitivity estimates using the Hamburg 14 T solenoid
sections.caveat: No gravitational-wave signal is reported. Sensitivity depends on noise and readout performance; cryogenic and SQUID upgrades are future improvements.

sections.title: First Detection of the Doppler Shift of X-ray Photons Due to a Telescope’s Orbital Motion
sections.abstract: The authors analyze XRISM/Resolve observations of narrow Galactic-centre Fe Kα lines and report orbital redshift modulation at 95% confidence.
sections.claimed_result: The authors find evidence for red/blue modulation correlated with XRISM’s orbital motion in several observations; the arXiv metadata reports ApJ acceptance.
sections.evidence_type: observational; XRISM/Resolve spectra of narrow iron Kα emission from Galactic-centre molecular clouds
sections.caveat: The reported confidence is 95%, not a discovery-level significance; the result is based on a small set of observations and depends on ruling out instrument/systematic alternatives.

sections.title: Detection of fine-structured radio bursts during a superflare on EQ Peg
sections.abstract: Combining FAST radio data with TESS optical observations, the authors report short, highly polarized radio spikes coincident with a 2022 superflare on the M-dwarf binary EQ Peg, consistent with coherent emission such as the electron-cyclotron maser.
sections.claimed_result: The spikes lasted roughly 100 s, had brightness temperatures above 10¹³ K and circular polarization around 0.84 ± 0.16; the authors argue these features favor coherent emission and connect the radio bursts to the flare.
sections.evidence_type: observational; FAST radio and TESS optical data, interpreted with Zeeman–Doppler imaging of EQ Peg
sections.caveat: This is one flare observed in 2022, and source locations rely on an assumed large-scale dipolar magnetic field; the proposed emission mechanism is an interpretation, not a direct identification.

sections.title: Real-Time String Dynamics in 3+1D Lattice Quantum Electrodynamics
sections.abstract: Tree-tensor-network simulations model real-time string breaking in 3+1D U(1) lattice QED, resolving resonant pair creation and competing off-resonant channels.
sections.claimed_result: At strong coupling, the simulated electric string breaks resonantly into matter–antimatter pairs; away from resonance, pair production, string deformations, extensions and flux loops deplete the string sector.
sections.evidence_type: computational; tree tensor networks and channel-resolved perturbation theory for a U(1) lattice-gauge model
sections.caveat: This is a numerical U(1) gauge-theory simulation and a benchmark for future quantum simulators, not an observation of real-time QCD; extrapolation to QCD requires further work.

sections.title: Nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence in tau-lepton pairs from electron–positron collisions
sections.abstract: The authors propose a single-observable witness for nonlocal advantage of quantum coherence (NAQC) in tau-pair production at Belle II and a future FCC-ee collider, and estimate the precision needed to test it.
sections.claimed_result: Their calculation estimates that a 5σ NAQC observation would require about 1% precision at Belle II and a few-percent precision at FCC-ee; this is a sensitivity forecast, not an observed collider result.
sections.evidence_type: theoretical; quantum-correlation calculations and proposed analyses at 10.58 GeV (Belle II) and 91.19 GeV (FCC-ee)
sections.caveat: The result is contingent on experimental precision and implementation of the proposed witness/steering-game protocol; the paper does not report a new measurement.

sections.title: System-size dependence of bottomonium suppression from Pb-Pb to light-ion collisions
sections.abstract: The authors apply the same open-quantum-system transport coefficients to Pb-Pb, O-O and Ne-Ne collisions and compare predicted bottomonium suppression with CMS and LHCb measurements.
sections.claimed_result: Without retuning microscopic transport coefficients, the model reproduces the O-O suppression hierarchy and magnitude; the authors say current Ne-Ne data favor somewhat stronger suppression than predicted.
sections.evidence_type: computational; QTraj solution of an NLO pNRQCD Lindblad equation in anisotropic hydrodynamic backgrounds, compared with CMS/LHCb measurements
sections.caveat: Ne-Ne experimental uncertainties remain large, and the calculation uses smooth optical-Glauber initial conditions; the authors call for event-by-event fluctuating initial conditions.
